kev_new.vulnerabilityName: Perforce Puppet Enterprise Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability
kev_new.shortDescription: Perforce Puppet Enterprise contains a deserialization of untrusted data vulnerability in Puppet’s report-processing code that allows a client with any CA-signed agent certificate to execute arbitrary code on the Puppet Server as the service user by submitting a report containing a crafted rich-data type through a PUT request. If the certificate authority automatically signs requests without strong verification, an unauthenticated network attacker can obtain a valid certificate and exploit the vulnerability.
kev_new.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

kev_new.vulnerabilityName: Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) Code Injection Vulnerability
kev_new.shortDescription: Vanderbilt University Research Electronic Data Capture (REDCap) contains a code injection vulnerability which could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the server. An attacker could exploit this via crafted HTTP requests that access an unintended controller route from a public survey context and supply a crafted file-path or stream parameter during data import processing. Exploitation requires knowledge of a valid public survey hash.

FLTK through 1.4.5 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in Fl_BMP_Image::load_bmp_() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory by supplying crafted BMP or ICO files. Attackers can specify very large image dimensions so the 32-bit row and alpha mask pointer offsets wrap, writing file-derived pixel bytes out of bounds to crash applications or possibly execute code.

Daptin before 0.13.61 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to overwrite restricted contacts by sending CardDAV PUT requests to existing contacts. Attackers holding address book Update permission can bypass per-contact row permissions in PutAddressObject to modify protected contacts and confirm their existence.

MediaInfoLib before 26.10 contains a heap use-after-free vulnerability in the Vorbis setup header parser that allows attackers to trigger reads of freed memory via crafted files. Attackers can supply a crafted Ogg/Vorbis file that makes File_Vorbis::Setup() return early without BS_End_LE(), leaving a stale bitstream pointer that causes crashes or heap disclosure.

MediaInfoLib before 26.10 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the MPEG-4 Visual parser that allows attackers to read global memory via an uninitialized frame_rate_code index into Mpegv_frame_rate. Attackers can supply a crafted MP4 file that forces stream finalization before parser synchronization, crashing the process or leaking adjacent memory into the reported frame rate.

MediaInfoLib before 26.10 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in File_Mpegv::Streams_Fill() that allows attackers to read adjacent memory via an uninitialized chroma_format index. Attackers can craft media files that reach Streams_Fill() before Synched_Init(), crashing MediaInfo or embedding applications and possibly exposing static memory in parser output.
